extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of affected electric generating units (Entergy, AEP, AECC), state environmental agencies (ADEQ), environmental groups, and members of the public who submit comments on EPA rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register proposed rule by EPA proposing to extend NOx compliance deadlines in the Arkansas Regional Haze Federal Implementation Plan (FIP) and providing procedural instructions for petitions, public comments, and hearings related to that proposed revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received on or before September 22, 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document specifies a firm close date for receipt of comments; submissions received after this date will not be timely. (Published Content - Document Dates: Comments must be received on or before September 22, 2017.)

rubrics_metrics.name: How to identify and submit comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your comments, identified by Docket No. EPA-R06-OAR-2015-0189, at http://www.regulations.gov or via email to R6AIR_ARHaze@epa.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online instructions for submitting comments. Once submitted, comments cannot be edited or removed from Regulations.gov. For additional submission methods, contact the listed EPA staff. Include docket number to ensure comments are associated with the correct rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) and sensitive material
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit electronically any information you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA may publish any comment received to its public docket; some submissions may be redacted or withheld. Some docket materials may be publicly available only at the hard copy location (e.g., copyrighted material).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia submissions requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written comment is considered the official comment and should include discussion of all points you wish to make. EPA will generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing system).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary submission requirement (no external links)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all substantive material is included directly in the Regulations.gov submission or email; do not rely on external links as the primary vehicle for arguments or supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket access and hard-copy materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The index to the docket for this action is available electronically at www.regulations.gov and in hard copy at the EPA Region 6 office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While all documents are listed in the index, some information may be publicly available only at the hard copy location (e.g., copyrighted material), and some may not be publicly available at either location (e.g., CBI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing and information session procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The public hearing will provide interested parties the opportunity to present information and opinions; an information session will be held to provide additional information and informal discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written statements and supporting information submitted during the comment period will be considered with the same weight as any oral comments and supporting information presented at the public hearing. EPA staff will be available during the information session to informally answer questions, but comments made there must still be submitted orally at the hearing or formally in writing within 30 days after completion of the hearings to be part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral comments treated equivalently to written comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Written statements and supporting information submitted during the comment period will be considered with the same weight as any oral comments and supporting information presented at the public hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim English language transcripts of the hearing and written statements will be included in the rulemaking docket. EPA will provide written responses to all significant oral and written comments received when publishing the final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing time limits and presentation restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: At the public hearings, the hearing officer may limit the time available for each commenter to address the proposal to three minutes or less if appropriate; EPA will not provide equipment for overhead slides or computerized slide presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan oral remarks to fit a potential short time allotment and bring any supporting materials in written form for the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to formalize informal information-session input
rubrics_metrics.description: Any comments made to EPA staff during an information session must still be provided orally during the public hearing, or formally in writing within 30 days after completion of the hearings, in order to be considered in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal exchanges at information sessions are not part of the official record unless repeated at the hearing or submitted in writing within the stated timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA notice on publication status and legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a 'Web 2.0' version of the daily Federal Register; it is not an official legal edition and does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For legal research or to cite the official document, use the PDF on govinfo.gov; verify contents against the official edition for legal notice and judicial notice under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of public comment for this proposed action
rubrics_metrics.description: The revisions to the Arkansas Regional Haze FIP proposed at this time are limited to the NOx compliance dates for the five aforementioned units. EPA is not accepting public comment at this time on any issues unrelated to the NOx compliance dates for these units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be focused on the proposed extension of NOx compliance deadlines; unrelated matters will not be considered in this specific proceeding (other portions of the FIP may be reconsidered separately).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for granting reconsideration under CAA section 307(d)(7)(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA determined that the petitioners raised objections to the NOx compliance timeframes that were impracticable to raise during the comment period and that are of central relevance to the rule under 307(d)(7)(B) of the Clean Air Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To warrant reconsideration, EPA looks for objections that could not reasonably have been raised earlier and that are central to the rule; such objections can trigger administrative stay and reconsideration procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory BART timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with CAA section 169A(b)(2) and (g)(4) and the Regional Haze Rule under section 51.308(e)(1)(iv): install and operate BART as expeditiously as practicable, but in no event later than 5 years after approval of the implementation plan revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When setting compliance deadlines for Best Available Retrofit Technology (BART), EPA must balance expeditious installation with practical constraints, but cannot exceed the 5-year statutory maximum from approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors EPA considers when assessing feasibility of a compliance deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Site-specific considerations that can affect installation and deployment time of low NOx burner controls, including permitting timelines, companies' internal project development and approval processes, vendor selection and fabrication lead times, outage scheduling, installation durations, tuning/testing, and staff training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA accepted petitioners' assertions that the 18-month deadline did not account for PSD permitting (which may take 6–8 months or longer and can be delayed by public comment or appeal), internal prudence reviews and competitive bidding, vendor design/fabrication (~8 months), unit outages (~6–7 weeks per unit), boiler tuning, performance verification testing, fine-tuning, and training. EPA may extend compliance deadlines where such site-specific, procedural, or reliability considerations make a shorter deadline infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of electric system reliability and coordinated scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Scheduling installations across multiple units in the same regional transmission organization must account for system reliability and replacement energy costs; accelerated schedules could compromise reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA recognized that optimal scheduling to minimize replacement energy costs and preserve reliability may require longer compliance schedules, particularly when several affected units are within the same transmission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of petitions and scope of possible revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will consider petitions for reconsideration and, if warranted, propose revisions; revisions proposed here are limited to NOx compliance dates but the ongoing reconsideration could result in future rulemaking for other portions of the FIP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should submit site-specific information and arguments showing why reconsideration is warranted; EPA may address other issues separately if reconsideration shows other parts need revision.
